tagline: Down the river of sand, the way the pine went.
intro: The byway starts on M-65 near Loud Dam Pond and runs east through the Huron National Forest, then turns off onto River Road and keeps to the south bank of the Au Sable. It stays by the water past one dam pond after another into Oscoda, a few blocks short of Lake Huron.

The river was the road first. In the late 1800s white pine floated down it to the sawmills at the mouth. When the pine was gone, power dams went in during the 1920s, and the water stands behind them still.

moments.title: Iargo Springs
moments.text: Stairs go down to boardwalks over springs that early loggers dammed to water their camps, back when most of Cooke Pond below was dry land.

moments.title: Lumberman's Monument
moments.text: A timber cruiser with his compass, a sawyer and a river rat leaning on his peavey stand in bronze above Cooke Dam Pond, where the logs once went by.

moments.title: Oscoda
moments.text: The Au Sable canoe marathon finishes here after 120 miles and a night on the river, and the state counts the town as the official home of Paul Bunyan.
